Kuvitus: koulun työpöydällä on kytkentäl: Illustration: on a school workbench there is a breadboard. On the left is a battery holder with three AA batteries, from which a red and a black wire run to the breadboard. On the board there is a resistor and two red LEDs. The first LED shines brightly; the second, identical LED is connected the other way round and does not light. In the background, outside a window, the sun is shining, and on the windowsill there is a small solar panel.
Kaksi kytkentäkaaviota vierekkäin, ei mi: Two circuit diagrams side by side, not to scale. In each, a voltage source U, a series resistor R and a red LED are in series, and the positive terminal of the source is at the top. On the left the triangle of the LED points downwards, in the direction of the current: the anode of the LED is above, towards the positive terminal of the source, and the cathode, the bar, below. The LED shines, and purple arrows show the current I flowing from the positive terminal through the resistor and the LED to the negative terminal. This is the forward direction. On the right the same LED has been turned round, and the triangle points upwards. The LED does not shine, and no current flows in the circuit: I = 0. This is the reverse direction.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa, laskettu luvun di: Graph to scale, calculated with the diode model of the chapter: the current I of a diode in milliamperes as a function of its voltage U_D in volts, the voltage ranging from −2 V to 4 V and the current from 0 to 30 mA. At negative voltages, that is, in the reverse direction, the current is zero for all three components. In the forward direction the current of the silicon diode stays almost zero up to about 0.6 volts and then rises steeply, and a current of 10 milliamperes is reached at 0.70 volts. The curve of the red LED rises steeply from about 1.8 volts, and 10 mA is reached at 1.9 volts. The curve of the blue LED rises from about 2.8 volts, and 10 mA is reached at 2.9 volts. The grid spacings are 1 V and 5 mA.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa, laskettu luvun au: Graph to scale, calculated with the solar panel model of the chapter: the current I of a small solar panel in milliamperes as a function of its voltage U in volts at two light intensities. When the light intensity G is 1000 W/m², the curve starts on the vertical axis at the short-circuit current I_sc = 200 mA, stays almost horizontal up to about four volts and then falls steeply to the horizontal axis at the open-circuit voltage U_oc = 6.0 V. When the light intensity is 500 W/m², the short-circuit current is half, 100 mA, but the open-circuit voltage is 5.7 V, only a little smaller. The grid spacings are 1 V and 50 mA.
Vasemmalla kytkentäkaavio, ei mittakaava: On the left a circuit diagram, not to scale: a voltage source U, a series resistor R and an LED in series, the LED in the forward direction. A purple arrow shows the current I flowing from the positive terminal of the source through the resistor and the LED to the negative terminal. The voltage of the resistor is U_R and the voltage of the LED U_D. On the right a bar to scale: the voltage of the source, 6.0 V, is divided into a resistor voltage of 4.0 V and an LED voltage of 2.0 V, so U = U_R + U_D.
Kaksi kuvaajaa mittakaavassa yhteisellä: Two graphs to scale with a common voltage axis, calculated with the solar panel model of the chapter at a light intensity of 1000 W/m². Upper: the current I of the panel in milliamperes as a function of the voltage U, the curve running from 200 mA to 6.0 volts. At 5.0 V and 184 mA there is a point, and the rectangle between it and the origin is shaded orange: its area is the power P = U I. Lower: the power P in watts as a function of the voltage. The power is zero in a short circuit and at open circuit and greatest, about 0.92 W, when the voltage is about 5.0 V. A dashed line joins the maximum power points of both graphs.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: vihreän LEDin vir: Graph to scale: the current I of a green LED in milliamperes as a function of its voltage U_D in volts. The grid spacing of the horizontal axis is 0.2 V and the numbers are marked at 0.4 volt intervals; the grid spacing of the vertical axis is 5 mA. The current is almost zero up to about two volts, after which the curve rises steeply and ends at 30 milliamperes a little to the right of 2.2 volts.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: aurinkopaneelin v: Graph to scale: the current I of a solar panel in milliamperes as a function of its voltage U in volts when the light intensity stays the same. The grid spacings are 1 V and 50 mA. The curve starts on the vertical axis at 200 milliamperes, stays almost horizontal up to about four volts, bends down at about five volts and falls steeply to the horizontal axis at six volts.
